target_customer: Southeast Asia e-commerce sellers, especially those sourcing products from China, who pay for fulfillment
problem: Cross border sourcing, storage, pick and pack and delivery for small online sellers was costly and fragmented. The company claimed cross border logistics could take up to 45 percent of a product's capital.
business_model: Fulfillment as a service with no upfront fee, charged per order and service
product_category: E-commerce fulfillment and cross border logistics

founders.name: Ng Yi Ying
education: Master's degree at Tsinghua University (pursuing when she met her co-founder in 2012)
previous_startups: Online business sourcing products from China to sell in Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand

founders.name: Liu Yi Shu
previous_startups: Online business sourcing products from China to sell in Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand
founders.background_notes: Worked at Amazon China when they met, per e27.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed order management software linking virtual warehouses in China and Malaysia plus real logistics operations, at 120,000 parcels a day claimed capacity.

defensibility.rationale: The warehouse network of 250 virtual warehouses and seller integrations gave some stickiness, but fulfillment was a competitive commodity with many regional providers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copy was reported. The company remains active and rebranded its site to allsome.io.

market_need_then: Southeast Asian e-commerce was growing fast in 2019 and small sellers sourcing from China faced high cross border logistics cost. The company claimed 50 clients and 250 virtual warehouses at its seed announcement (e27, August 2019).

branding.domain_note: Site allsome.com redirects (301) to allsome.io, observed during research.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain B2B claims such as 99.99 percent on time shipping and 50 percent cost saving

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself was found, only funding and founder coverage. The name is generic.

outcome_analysis: AllSome raised a US$1.94M seed round led by East Ventures in August 2019 after YC and expanded toward Indonesia. It is still listed as active with about 18 people, so the outcome is unresolved. No later funding was found in the sources, and the company appears to have stayed small and capital light. Its fate depends on whether fulfillment as a service can reach scale against many regional logistics providers.
notes: Seed of US$1.94M is stated by e27, DailySocial and Bisnis (Rp27.7 billion), investor list from search summary of DailySocial. CB Insights total of $2.24M over 4 rounds is an unverified aggregator figure, so earlier pre-seed rounds are not recorded. Company site returned a redirect and the new site fetch gave no content. Competitor names seen (Flash Fulfillment, Red Stag, iStore iSend, TresGo) came from aggregator pages with no 2019 date, so none are listed. No outcome news found. Founding year conflicts (2017 on CB Insights, 2018 elsewhere).
